# Crypto / privacy review — PR #899 (`feat/803-snapshot-adapter-login-handoff`)

Scope: `apps/web/src/engine/loginHandoff.ts`, its test, `createEngineClient.ts`, `auth.store.ts`, `packages/client/src/index.ts`, plus the paths this PR newly activates (`engineClient.ts`, `transport.ts`, `worker/engineHost.ts`, `crates/engine/src/session.rs`).

Verdict: the zeroization chain is essentially correct and the guard is right. One HIGH finding — a global, synchronously-readable copy of the login secret created inside `fromHex` — and one MEDIUM on the failover path this PR turns on.

---

## [HIGH] `fromHex`'s regex validation parks the full login secret in V8's globally readable RegExp legacy statics

**Location:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-ad37e60adbb2b2699/packages/client/src/seams/bytes.ts:26`, reached from `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-ad37e60adbb2b2699/apps/web/src/engine/loginHandoff.ts:27`

```ts
// bytes.ts:26
if (!/^[0-9a-fA-F]*$/.test(hex)) {
```

**Issue:** `RegExp.prototype.test` updates the Annex B legacy statics on a successful match. Since the pattern is anchored and matches the whole string, `RegExp.input` / `RegExp['$_']` / `RegExp.lastMatch` / `RegExp['$&']` are all set to the entire secret hex, and stay set until the next successful regex match anywhere in that realm. Verified on this machine's V8:

```
RegExp.input:     "00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff"
RegExp.lastMatch: "00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff"
```

V8, JSC and SpiderMonkey all implement these. `fromHex` was previously only fed opaque non-secret store keys (see the module header at `bytes.ts:1-8`); this PR makes it secret-bearing by re-exporting it (`packages/client/src/index.ts:35`) and pointing it at the TSS export.

**Impact:** the secp256k1 login scalar — the root of the whole key hierarchy — becomes readable with a single property get by *any* script sharing the UI-thread realm: Web3Auth/Torus, wagmi/viem and their transitive deps, an XSS payload, or an error-reporting shim that dumps globals. No timing, no heap-snapshot access needed. This defeats the module's own claim at `loginHandoff.ts:19` ("the decoded buffer is the only copy whose lifetime we control") and makes the transfer/zeroize discipline moot. Secondary: `Number.parseInt(hex.slice(i * 2, i * 2 + 2), 16)` at `bytes.ts:31` sprays 32 secret-bearing 2-char substrings across the heap.

**Recommendation:** make the one shared codec regex-free and substring-free — no second codec, no behavior change, and it fixes the seam callers too:

```ts
export function fromHex(hex: string): Uint8Array {
  if (hex.length % 2 !== 0) {
    throw new TypeError('fromHex: hex string must have an even length');
  }
  const out = new Uint8Array(hex.length / 2);
  for (let i = 0; i < out.length; i += 1) {
    const hi = nibble(hex.charCodeAt(i * 2));
    const lo = nibble(hex.charCodeAt(i * 2 + 1));
    if (hi < 0 || lo < 0) throw new TypeError('fromHex: hex string contains a non-hex character');
    out[i] = (hi << 4) | lo;
  }
  return out;
}

function nibble(code: number): number {
  if (code >= 0x30 && code <= 0x39) return code - 0x30; // 0-9
  if (code >= 0x61 && code <= 0x66) return code - 0x57; // a-f
  if (code >= 0x41 && code <= 0x46) return code - 0x37; // A-F
  return -1;
}
```

Add a regression test in `loginHandoff.test.ts`:

```ts
it('leaves no copy of the secret in the RegExp legacy statics', async () => {
  const { client } = transferringClient();
  await handOffLoginSecret(client, exporter(SECRET_HEX));
  for (const slot of [RegExp.input, RegExp.lastMatch, RegExp['$&']]) {
    expect(slot).not.toContain(SECRET_HEX.slice(0, 16));
  }
});
```

(That test fails today and passes with the fix — I confirmed the leak reproduces in plain V8.)

---

## [MEDIUM] Failover secret is never zeroed when promotion fails — a path this PR activates

**Location:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-ad37e60adbb2b2699/packages/client/src/engineClient.ts:210-213`

```ts
if (wasActiveFollower) {
  const secret = await this.provideFailoverSecret();
  await local.start(secret);
}
```

**Issue:** if `local.start` rejects — worker `ready` rejected, a `fatal` message, `close()` during startup, or a `postMessage` throw — control jumps to `abortPromotion` (`engineClient.ts:227-229`) and the buffer is never scrubbed. It is GC-eligible but not zeroed, so a live secp256k1 private key sits in the heap until a nondeterministic collection, exposed to heap snapshots and crash dumps. This contradicts the `SecretSource` contract stated at `engineClient.ts:34` ("transferred into the worker and zeroed — never retained"). `engineClient.ts` is not in the diff, but `createEngineClient.ts:25` (`secretSource: loginSecretSource`) plus `loginHandoff.ts:70-75` are what make this path live for the first time, so it belongs to this PR.

**Recommendation:** mirror the discipline `handOffLoginSecret` already uses:

```ts
if (wasActiveFollower) {
  const secret = await this.provideFailoverSecret();
  try {
    await local.start(secret);
  } finally {
    if (secret.byteLength > 0) new Uint8Array(secret).fill(0);
  }
}
```

Cover it in `packages/client/src/engineClient.test.ts` with a `secretSource` whose buffer you retain, a worker that fails `ready`, and an assertion that the retained buffer reads all zeros.

---

## [LOW] No 32-byte length check at the boundary — late-failing, but not fail-open

**Location:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-ad37e60adbb2b2699/apps/web/src/engine/loginHandoff.ts:32`

I checked both ends before scoring this:

- Rust fails closed. `crates/engine/src/session.rs:72-76` requires exactly `SECRET_LEN` (32) bytes via `try_into` and a valid in-range scalar via `EcdsaSigner::from_scalar`, returning `EngineError::InvalidSecret` otherwise (`facade.rs:481`), with negative tests at `session.rs:334` (31 bytes) and `session.rs:343` (all-zero). So accepting any non-empty length in TS is **not** a fail-open.
- The pinned Core Kit already pads. `@web3auth/mpc-core-kit@3.5.0` `mpcCoreKit.js:887` returns `tssKey.toString("hex", FIELD_ELEMENT_HEX_LEN)` with `FIELD_ELEMENT_HEX_LEN = 32 * 2` (`constants.js:45`), so the export is always 64 chars today. (v1 relied on this same unstated invariant — `v1:apps/web/src/lib/web3auth/hooks.ts:86`.)

Still worth an explicit check: it keeps malformed key material off the `postMessage` boundary entirely, and it converts a future Core Kit bump that drops the padding from an opaque engine `InvalidSecret` (after a cross-thread transfer) into a clear local error. A length invariant is not crypto-in-TS.

```ts
const LOGIN_SECRET_LEN = 32; // secp256k1 scalar; mirrors SECRET_LEN in crates/engine/src/session.rs
...
if (decoded.length !== LOGIN_SECRET_LEN) {
  decoded.fill(0);
  throw new Error('login secret export is not a 32-byte scalar');
}
```

Note the `decoded.fill(0)` before throwing — the current `length === 0` throw at line 32 leaves no residue (empty array), but a length-mismatch throw would abandon a populated buffer.

---

## [LOW] Test-quality gaps

**Location:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-ad37e60adbb2b2699/apps/web/src/engine/loginHandoff.test.ts`

I ran the suite (15/15 pass) and traced each assertion against the three mutations you asked about:

- **Remove the `finally` zeroization → CAUGHT.** `loginHandoff.test.ts:90-99` asserts `new Uint8Array(seen[0])` equals a 32-byte zero array on the reject path. Real assertion, real failure.
- **Remove the transfer → NOT caught here.** `loginHandoff.test.ts:78-86` ("leaves the sender buffer detached after the transfer") asserts `received[0].byteLength === 0`, but the detach is performed by the test double itself (`structuredClone(secret, { transfer: [secret] })` at line 26), not by production code. It proves only that `handOffLoginSecret` tolerates a detached buffer. The actual transfer contract *is* pinned — `packages/client/src/transport.test.ts:224-235` asserts `posted.transfer` equals `[secret]`, and the new `Web Unit` gate runs `@cipherbox/client` too (`ci.yml`) — so coverage exists; just don't read this test as the transfer gate. Rename it to something like "tolerates a buffer the transport already detached".
- **Start logging the secret → PARTIALLY caught.** `loginHandoff.test.ts:139` only greps for the lowercase hex. `console.log(new Uint8Array(secret))` (`"0,17,34,…"`), an uppercase re-encode, or a base64 dump all slip through. Since production logs nothing on this path, tighten to `expect(logged).toEqual([])` for the handoff, and add the decimal byte-join to the containment check.

**Vacuous assertion — name it:** `loginHandoff.test.ts:129`

```ts
await new LoginSecretSource().provideSecret().catch(() => undefined);
```

This constructs a source with no exporter, so it rejects at `loginHandoff.ts:72` without ever touching a secret. It contributes nothing to the storage/log assertions that follow. Fix:

```ts
const source = new LoginSecretSource();
source.use(exporter(SECRET_HEX));
await source.provideSecret();
```

Two missing cases worth adding: (a) a real `EngineClient` in the `role === 'closed'` state — `engineClient.ts:114` rejects *before* its own zeroing at line 120, so this is precisely the case where `handOffLoginSecret`'s `finally` is the only scrubber; (b) a `start` that throws synchronously rather than returning a rejected promise.

`expect(localStorage.length).toBe(0)` (lines 136-137, and `auth.store.test.ts:56-57`) is weak — it can only catch a write made by these two modules — but it is cheap; keep it.

---

## Cleared — explicit findings of nothing

**Zeroization chain (Q1): correct, and the `byteLength > 0` guard is the right discipline.** Full audit:

| Copy | Fate |
|---|---|
| Core Kit BN + returned hex string | uncontrollable, GC-only (correctly acknowledged at `loginHandoff.ts:18`) |
| `exported.slice(2)` string | uncontrollable, GC-only |
| `RegExp` legacy statics | **leaked — the HIGH above** |
| `decoded: Uint8Array` | zeroed at `loginHandoff.ts:36` before return |
| `secret: ArrayBuffer`, leader path | transferred at `transport.ts:95` → detached → `byteLength === 0` → `finally` correctly skips. **No double-zero.** |
| `secret: ArrayBuffer`, follower path | zeroed by `engineClient.ts:120`, then zeroed again by `loginHandoff.ts:53`. Idempotent, harmless. |
| worker-side `Uint8Array` | `view.fill(0)` in a `finally` at `packages/client/src/worker/engineHost.ts:44-53` |
| Rust | `LoginSecret(Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>)` (`facade.rs:223`) with a redacted `Debug` (`facade.rs:245-248`) |

Keep the `finally`: `engineClient.ts:114` (`role === 'closed'`) rejects without zeroing, so `EngineClient` is *not* an unconditional terminal owner and `handOffLoginSecret` is the only backstop for that exit. The redundant follower-path double-zero is not the harmful direction of the callee-must-not-zero rule (`EngineClient.start` declares itself terminal owner at `engineClient.ts:115-119`); no buffer is scrubbed out from under a caller that still needs it. Also confirmed `BroadcastTransport.start()` (`broadcastTransport.ts:59-62`) ignores the argument entirely — no secret ever crosses the BroadcastChannel.

**Rule 4 — no crypto/codec in TS (Q2): not violated.** Nothing in `loginHandoff.ts` derives, signs, seals, or compares key material; all derivation stays in `session.rs:72-83`. Hex is a transport encoding, not a cryptographic operation, and the PR routes it through the single existing codec via `packages/client/src/index.ts:35` rather than growing a second one — which is the right call. The `0x` strip is canonicalizing a third-party encoding, same class. Moving the decode into Rust would not help: the string is already in the JS heap by then, and you would still cross the worker boundary with either a string (worse — strings are not transferable, so it would be *copied*) or bytes (identical to today).

**Side channels (Q3): no meaningful timing channel; error paths leak nothing.** `fromHex` is data-dependent in time, but there is no attacker-supplied comparand, no oracle, and no repeat-query surface — it is a one-shot local decode of a locally-held secret. The real "side channel" in this file is memory residency, covered by the HIGH. ## [HIGH] `fromHex`'s regex validation parks the full login secret in V8's globally readable RegExp legacy statics

**Location:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-ad37e60adbb2b2699/packages/client/src/seams/bytes.ts:26`, reached from `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-ad37e60adbb2b2699/apps/web/src/engine/loginHandoff.ts:27`

```ts
// bytes.ts:26
if (!/^[0-9a-fA-F]*$/.test(hex)) {
```

**Issue:** `RegExp.prototype.test` updates the Annex B legacy statics on a successful match. Since the pattern is anchored and matches the whole string, `RegExp.input` / `RegExp['$_']` / `RegExp.lastMatch` / `RegExp['$&']` are all set to the entire secret hex, and stay set until the next successful regex match anywhere in that realm. Verified on this machine's V8:

```
RegExp.input:     "00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff"
RegExp.lastMatch: "00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff"
```

V8, JSC and SpiderMonkey all implement these. `fromHex` was previously only fed opaque non-secret store keys (see the module header at `bytes.ts:1-8`); this PR makes it secret-bearing by re-exporting it (`packages/client/src/index.ts:35`) and pointing it at the TSS export.

**Impact:** the secp256k1 login scalar — the root of the whole key hierarchy — becomes readable with a single property get by *any* script sharing the UI-thread realm: Web3Auth/Torus, wagmi/viem and their transitive deps, an XSS payload, or an error-reporting shim that dumps globals. No timing, no heap-snapshot access needed. This defeats the module's own claim at `loginHandoff.ts:19` ("the decoded buffer is the only copy whose lifetime we control") and makes the transfer/zeroize discipline moot. Secondary: `Number.parseInt(hex.slice(i * 2, i * 2 + 2), 16)` at `bytes.ts:31` sprays 32 secret-bearing 2-char substrings across the heap.

**Recommendation:** make the one shared codec regex-free and substring-free — no second codec, no behavior change, and it fixes the seam callers too:

```ts
export function fromHex(hex: string): Uint8Array {
  if (hex.length % 2 !== 0) {
    throw new TypeError('fromHex: hex string must have an even length');
  }
  const out = new Uint8Array(hex.length / 2);
  for (let i = 0; i < out.length; i += 1) {
    const hi = nibble(hex.charCodeAt(i * 2));
    const lo = nibble(hex.charCodeAt(i * 2 + 1));
    if (hi < 0 || lo < 0) throw new TypeError('fromHex: hex string contains a non-hex character');
    out[i] = (hi << 4) | lo;
  }
  return out;
}

function nibble(code: number): number {
  if (code >= 0x30 && code <= 0x39) return code - 0x30; // 0-9
  if (code >= 0x61 && code <= 0x66) return code - 0x57; // a-f
  if (code >= 0x41 && code <= 0x46) return code - 0x37; // A-F
  return -1;
}
```


## 1. `VAULT_ROOT_NODE_ID` — wrong altitude, and the deep fix is far cheaper than assumed

`apps/web/src/engine/snapshotStore.ts:15` — a TS-side literal re-asserts an engine-internal bootstrap anchor — **fix it deeper; recommend the wire change.**

The premise that the deep fix costs "Rust + worker protocol + transport + facade" is only two-thirds true. The Rust side is already done:

- `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1695` already exposes `pub fn root(&self) -> NodeId`, doc'd as "the FUSE mount anchor. The seeded all-zero root until cold-start/resolve **replaces the base snapshot**."
- `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1026` (`*self.snapshot.borrow_mut() = outcome.base;`) is the replacement point. The all-zero id survives today only because `start()` threads it in at facade.rs:972 → `cold_start_data_path(..., root)`. That is an implementation coincidence, not a contract.
- `SnapshotDescriptor.root` already crosses the wire (`packages/client/src/worker/protocol.ts:61`), and `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs:819` asserts `view.root() == vec![1u8; 16]` — a **non-zero** root — so the wasm layer already treats the root as data, not a constant.

The only real gap is the bootstrap call: `crates/wasm/src/host.rs:235` takes `folder: &NodeId` with no "the root" option, so TS must name a folder before it has ever seen one.

Concrete cost of the shallow version: `snapshot(folder)` returns `Err(EngineError::UnknownNode)` for an unrendered id (facade.rs:1457). If the adopted base ever roots at anything but all-zero — a shared scope, or any change at facade.rs:972/1026 — the very first pull rejects, and the UI shows a bare error string where the vault should be. No Rust test can catch it; the constant lives in a language the engine cannot see. Meanwhile `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:229` does `self.inodes.bind_root(view.root())` — the desktop host **asks**, the web host **guesses**. That asymmetry is precisely what "one core, two hosts" exists to prevent.

It also sits against `blueprint/web-client.md` "UI state law": *"Routes key on the stable node id — never `ipnsName` … and **no `'root'` sentinel**; the root is just the vault pointer's current root node."* An exported `VAULT_ROOT_NODE_ID` is a root sentinel, now reachable by every route module.

`apps/web/src/engine/snapshotStore.ts:90,121,132` — `describe(error)` collapses a classified engine error to a display string, discarding `EngineRequestError.code`.

`packages/client/src/correlatedTransport.ts:26-33` carries the engine's stable machine-readable code (`'unknownNode'`, `'contentUnavailable'`, …) end to end; the transport (`transport.ts:72`, `broadcastTransport.ts:138`) and the relay (`leaderRelay.ts:29`) all preserve it. `blueprint/web-client.md` "UI state law" requires *"Trust violations and withheld-update escalations render as a distinct warning class, never as staleness."* With only `error: string | null`, the UI's only future recourse is string-matching the message — the exact bandaid the state law exists to forbid. **#803 is done — PR #899**, draft, mergeable, +1167/−42 across 19 files, 17 checks green. Verified independently. I milestoned **#900** to v2.0.0 (it was filed labelled but unmilestoned, and it blocks #805, which is exactly the "gating the milestone from outside it" class we swept earlier).

**The find worth your attention is real, and it's the kind of thing that survives a normal review.** `fromHex` validated its input with `/^[0-9a-fA-F]*$/.test(hex)` — which populates `RegExp.input` and `RegExp.lastMatch`, realm-global statics, with the entire secp256k1 scalar. Any script sharing the UI realm could read the login secret straight off `RegExp`. That nullifies the whole transfer-and-zeroize discipline the slice exists to build. It's rewritten to decode by character code, the fix landed in `packages/client` so the seams benefit too, and there's a test asserting `RegExp.input` still reads `'sentinel'` after a login. I confirmed on the branch that no regex hex-validation remains in the production path — the only matches left are that test.

Second fix: the failover promotion never zeroed its re-derived secret when the promoted worker failed before `ready`. This PR is what makes that path reachable, so it correctly belongs here.

**One deviation to rule on**, same shape as #867's: the issue's gate says "web unit", and the worker initially added a `Web Unit` CI job — then deleted it, because root `pnpm test` is `pnpm -r --if-present run test` and both packages define `test`, so the existing **`Test`** job already runs them and already blocks merges. It named `Test` in `blueprint/testing.md`'s gate table instead, and corrected a blueprint line that wrongly claimed `apps/web` has no unit suite. Testing law 1 wants *a* named merge-blocking gate, not necessarily a new one — I think that's right, but it's a deliberate departure from the literal wording.

No Puppeteer pass, honestly reported: this slice renders nothing, `LoginPage`/`FilesPage` are still #883 placeholders, and there's no login flow to drive until #804. Manual steps are in the PR body.

Rationale, stated once in `encode.rs`'s rustdoc: a grow-from-empty `Vec` frees each intermediate backing store un-zeroized, stranding secret bytes in freed heap.

**`/resolve-pr-reviews #898` is running** as a dedicated worker with the full flow (fetch → triage → fix → reply → resolve → report). It's briefed on the two places findings hide in this repo: CodeRabbit puts nitpicks in the **review body** inside collapsed `<details>` blocks, not just inline threads, and `greptile-apps` is a second reviewer that often lands later — so it'll re-sweep near the end.

The four findings so far, all "Quick win" severity:

| Where | Finding |
|---|---|
| `write_plane.rs:1739` | `filter_map(...).ok()` makes three `retire_targets(...).is_empty()` assertions vacuous — a changed body shape would silently yield no targets and pass |
| `drain.rs:1583` | `only_a_quota_coded_413_blocks_and_every_other_413_is_permanent` asserts the *opposite* of its name — a code-less 413 yields `Halt::Attempt`, not `Permanent` |
| `wasm/src/host.rs:292` | data-integrity nit |
| `worker/protocol.ts:54` | doc comment conflates dead letters with retained records |

Two of those are worth more than their "nitpick" label: the vacuous-assertion one and the contradictory test name both sit on the fail-closed 413 path, and this repo's path instructions treat tests as the normative record of the blueprint rule. The misnamed test is also a direct artifact of the AC deviation I flagged earlier — the worker changed the behaviour so a code-less 413 takes a bounded number of attempts, but left the old name asserting "permanent". So the fix is a rename, and it confirms the deviation was deliberate rather than accidental.

**#893 is resuming** on its existing worktree rather than starting over — it had implementation plus `/simplify` done, and stopped before `/security-review` and `/crypto-privacy-review`. The fresh worker is told to establish state from disk first rather than trust the dead run's last message.

### 1. Fail-closed / error precedence — the key question. **Verified sound.**

`merged_len` (`fields.rs:87`) does now run before the `UnknownFieldCollision` check (`fields.rs:98`). The precedence *does* change, but it is not exploitable and cannot fail open. Proof of the directional property:

- Old-`Ok` ⟹ the loop ran `write_value` on every known entry ⟹ `merged_len` is `Ok`. So **no previously-accepted input is newly rejected**, and `merged_len` returning `Ok` skips none of the loop's checks, so **no previously-rejected input is newly accepted**.

The one observable delta: an input that *both* collides on a key *and* carries an over-deep known value now always returns `depth-exceeded`; before, it returned whichever fired first in canonical key order. Both are `Malformed` rejects. Nothing branches on this — `grep` shows the only consumers of `unknown-field-collision` are `error.rs`'s string table and `fields.rs:219` (shallow values, unaffected); `kat_manifest.rs:1369` explicitly documents that check as unit-test-pinned only. Deterministic precedence is arguably an improvement.

**Security bonus worth calling out:** because `merged_len` runs before *any* write, a `depth-exceeded` reject now drops an **empty** buffer instead of one already holding written secret bytes. That strictly extends the property #893 is about.

### 2. Integer overflow / DoS — **non-issue, and identical to pre-existing `encoded_len`.**

Every term in `merged_len` (`fields.rs:120-130`) is bounded by memory *already resident*: per entry, counted bytes are strictly less than resident bytes (`text_len(key)` = klen+≤9 vs `String` at 24+klen; `Bytes` n+≤9 vs `Vec` at 24+n; `Array`/`Map` contribute a ≤9-byte head vs a 24-byte `Vec` header; scalars 1–9 vs a ≥16-byte enum). `Value` has no `Rc`/`Arc`, so there is no aliasing amplification of counted-vs-resident. The sum therefore stays below the process's own live-heap footprint and cannot reach `usize::MAX` on 64-bit **or** on wasm32 (32-bit `usize`, 4 GiB linear-memory ceiling, and the `Map` must be materialized first). Same bound, same shape as `encoded_len` (`encode.rs:51`) — no new exposure. `merged_len` allocates nothing and sizes from fully-materialized inputs, so there's no "attacker declares a huge length" amplification (unlike a decoder length field). ### 1. Fail-closed / error precedence — the key question. **Verified sound.**

`merged_len` (`fields.rs:87`) does now run before the `UnknownFieldCollision` check (`fields.rs:98`). The precedence *does* change, but it is not exploitable and cannot fail open. Proof of the directional property:

- `count_value` (`encode.rs:57`) and `write_value` (`encode.rs:110`) both call `check_depth` at entry and recurse at `depth + 1`, over the same known values, at the same `MAP_ENTRY_DEPTH`. So `{values that make merged_len Err}` is exactly `{values that make the write loop Err}`.

The one observable delta: an input that *both* collides on a key *and* carries an over-deep known value now always returns `depth-exceeded`; before, it returned whichever fired first in canonical key order. content.text:
# Resolve PR Review Comments

Resolve all open review comments on the current PR from any automated reviewer (CodeRabbit, GitHub Copilot, etc.) or human reviewers.

## Workflow

### 1. Identify the PR

```bash
PR_NUMBER=$(gh pr view --json number --jq '.number')
```

If no PR exists for the current branch, stop and inform the user.

### 2. Fetch all unresolved review threads

Use the GraphQL `reviewThreads` query to get threads with `isResolved` status:

```bash
REPO_OWNER=$(gh repo view --json owner --jq '.owner.login')
REPO_NAME=$(gh repo view --json name --jq '.name')

gh api graphql -f query="
{
  repository(owner: \"$REPO_OWNER\", name: \"$REPO_NAME\") {
    pullRequest(number: $PR_NUMBER) {
      reviewThreads(first: 100) {
        nodes {
          id
          isResolved
          comments(first: 10) {
            nodes {
              id
              author { login }
              body
              path
              line
              createdAt
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}"
```

Filter to only unresolved threads. If none, report "No unresolved review threads" and stop.

### 3. Triage each comment

For each unresolved thread, read the comment and the referenced code. Categorize as:

- **Valid fix needed** — the comment identifies a real bug, security issue, or meaningful improvement
- **Already addressed** — the issue was fixed in a later commit on this branch
- **Not applicable** — the suggestion doesn't apply (explain why)

### 4. Implement fixes

For all "valid fix needed" comments:

1. Read the referenced file and understand the context
2. Implement the fix
3. Track which thread the fix addresses

Do NOT:

- Make unrelated changes or refactors
- Add features beyond what the comment requests
- Increase timeouts or add retries as a first approach — fix root causes

### 5. Run tests locally

After ALL fixes are implemented:

```bash
# Type check
pnpm typecheck

# Run relevant unit tests
pnpm test

# If E2E-relevant changes were made, run E2E tests too
cd tests/e2e && pnpm exec playwright test
```

Do NOT proceed to commit until tests pass. If tests fail, fix the failures first.

### 6. Commit and push

```bash
git add <specific-files>
git commit -m "fix: address PR review comments"
git push
```

### 7. Reply to and resolve each thread

For each thread, reply explaining what was done, then resolve:

- **Fixed comments**: Reply with what was changed and where, then resolve
- **Already addressed**: Reply explaining which commit addressed it, then resolve
- **Not applicable**: Reply with clear reasoning for not making changes, then resolve

Reply via REST (use `--field` not `-f` for `in_reply_to` — must be integer):

```bash
gh api repos/$REPO_OWNER/$REPO_NAME/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/comments \
  --field in_reply_to=COMMENT_ID \
  --raw-field body='...'
```

Resolve via GraphQL (can batch multiple):

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='
mutation {
  resolveReviewThread(input: {threadId: "THREAD_ID"}) {
    thread { isResolved }
  }
}'
```

### 8. Report summary

Print a summary table:

- Thread count resolved
- Fixes made (with file:line references)
- Comments marked as already addressed or not applicable

content.text:
**#899 is clean — 0 unresolved threads**, MERGEABLE at `09eb7f5a4`. Verified the `bytes.ts` scrub is genuinely on the branch, not just claimed.

**The `bytes.ts` finding was real, and it's the third key-disclosure bug this one slice has produced.** `fromHex` allocated `out` before the loop, so a non-hex character at position *2i* threw with the secp256k1 scalar's leading plaintext bytes still sitting in `out[0..i-1]` — and the caller's `catch` has no handle on that buffer to scrub it. It's now `out.fill(0, 0, i)` before the throw. The worker verified the live path (`exportLoginSecret` → `fromHex` carries the Core Kit scalar) rather than pattern-matching, and correctly noted the odd-length guard returns before `out` exists, so there's no leak on that branch.

The `auth.store` immutability finding was also real: `getState()` handed out the live object, and React bails out on identity — so a mutation would have been invisible to subscribers. Now `readonly` fields, a frozen `SIGNED_OUT`, and `Object.freeze(next)` on every `set()`.

Two judgement calls worth your eye, both declined-with-reasons rather than silently skipped:

**The `external-wallet` vocabulary request** — CodeRabbit wanted `LoginMethod` aligned to `VAULT_EXPORT_FORMAT.md`, but that doc's `method` domain is `web3auth | external-wallet` and can't distinguish Google from email, so `LoginMethod` isn't a subset of it. `docs/` is v1 legacy per AGENTS.md and vault import is cut in v2. It did remove the stale parenthetical that invited the cross-reference in the first place — that's the right residue to take from an otherwise-wrong suggestion.

**A test CodeRabbit asked for that can't exist** — it wanted an assertion that no non-zero bytes remain after a mid-string failure, but that buffer is never returned on the throw path. Observing it would require exporting it, which is a worse bug than the one being tested. The branch is already covered by the existing mid-string cases.

########## #868 ##########
engine: write file content end to end
Content bytes flow: sliced by the client, sealed and staged by the engine, uploaded at drain, published as a version. Gives `ApiClient::upload` its first production caller and the contract suite its first live write coverage. Slice settled by #825 on wayfinder map #813.

## Scope

**Facade write handles** (#815). The client slices the `File` and feeds chunks; the engine seals and stages each, owning framing policy; the op is journaled once at commit. Peak wasm heap is O(chunk). This replaces `Command::Create { content: Option<PlaintextContent> }` (`facade.rs:238-247`).

**Budget admission** (#828, #829). Reserve at `beginWrite` against an exact sealed total (`size + 40n + root_len`) in an in-memory ledger of live handles, so concurrent handles cannot over-admit. `pushChunk` enforces the declared shape and never re-checks the budget. The over-budget check quotes **`budget - staged`**, never `budget`, in distinct messages for the hard limit, a transient backlog, and a device-constrained budget — they need different user actions.

**Per-block staging** (#828). A version stages as N+1 independent blocks, each keyed by its own content address; the op carries the root's, which is also the version's `contentCid`. Leaf keys are derivable by decoding the staged root. Blocks are **CID-verified on read from staging** — the read path already hard-rejects a mismatch, so an unverified upload turns bit-rot into a permanently unreadable published version.

**The per-version content key** (#818). Staged sealed, HPKE-to-self under the owner `enc-subkey`, riding the op. `enc-subkey` comes from the loginSecret, so it is epoch-independent and availabl

########## #870 ##########
engine: publish and resolve the vault settings record
Vault settings become a published record on the network, resolvable with no CipherBox infrastructure. Settled by #825 on wayfinder map #813, overturning #822's `PUT/GET /account/settings`.

## Why

`AGENTS.md` commits to the network being canonical and CipherBox infra being accelerator-only. Holding `ByoIpfsConfig` on the API is circular: a self-hosting user would need CipherBox to tell them where their own node is. This is the pattern v1 shipped and it worked.

## Scope

- The settings record is published under the name derived from the new `settings-ipns-keypair` edge, and sealed **HPKE-to-self under `enc-subkey`** — v2's analogue of v1's ECIES-to-own-public-key. Both derive from `loginSecret`, so the record is readable at cold start **before any vault resolve**.
- Published through the shared publish port, so it inherits register-first, seq-CAS and confirm like every other record.
- **Tenants**: `ByoIpfsConfig` (`crates/engine/src/content/provider.rs:51`), `PinMode`, and the retention policy.
- **Harvest v1's semantics verbatim** from `apps/web/src/services/vault-settings.service.ts` on branch `v1`: validate the decoded payload, degrade gracefully to documented defaults on **any** failure, and bound the load with a timeout. A settings record that will not resolve must never block cold start.

## Constraint

The reserved settings id is a shared constant across accounts. The *keys* separate correctly, since the derivation is per-account through `loginSecret` — but the floor store keying is the exposed surface, and that hazard is #856's. Do not add a second instance of it.

## Acceptance

- Settings round-trip: wri

########## #635 ##########
engine: implement rotation primitives, sweep, name wave, and grants
## Scope

The three primitives with no recovery machinery: rotateScope (override seed mint, eager set law — owner cascade over every transitively-reachable descendant scope root fully rotated vs grantee flat self-contained, grant blobs re-wrapped verbatim for the committed set, owner blob, history link, ascent link, structure-signed by the rotator's writer pseudonym); sweep (idempotent epoch-lag work-list, epoch-converged pre-grant convergence, direct-child-scope index self-heal, metadata-only re-seal, idle-cadence Scheduler job, CAS-safe concurrent sweepers); rotateScopeWrite (commitment re-sign, write override seed, background child-first name wave with root re-pointed last, three-channel re-point publish, inventory swap via register-first and batch retire, root linger). The full trigger table including full-depth scope-exit detection, immediate-cut read revoke, write revoke/downgrade, discovered link expiry, manual rotate-now; grant creation (converge, mint scope at epoch 1, write-scope cut, parent index update, publish, mailbox share pointer) and invites (ephemeral-key blobs, bearer write-link flagging, claim conversion).
Does NOT land: scheduled hygiene rotation (designed-for, deferred).

## Blueprint anchors

`blueprint/engine.md`: Rotation primitives; Grants and ledger (grant creation, invites); Pointer planes (re-point publish)

## Gate

Engine simulation: the trigger table and eager-set law mirrored 1:1, sweep idempotence and concurrent sweepers, resumed name waves via the write-plane history link, crash-recovery from published records only, immediate cut, forgery-window bounds, grant-creation 

########## #752 ##########
engine: assemble the facade cold-start identity derivation and live-session wiring
Umbrella for completing the facade **cold-start sequence** — deriving the session identity and key material at login and assembling the live session behind the `Engine::start` surface.

## Context

`Engine::start` is currently the frozen facade skeleton (#623 scaffolded it; `lib.rs` / `facade.rs` note that "the full cold-start sequence … lands with the pipeline slices"). It authenticates and wires background work, but it does **not** yet derive the session identity/key material or assemble the live-session data paths. #739 (Closes #697) wired the liveness re-PUT loop into `start` but had to defer every piece that needs derived session key material or the live resolve path — see the dependent issues below.

## Scope

The cold-start sequence, end to end:

- Challenge-signature login → Web3Auth key derivation (per the auth pillar; #624 landed identity auth + refresh rotation).
- Session key material: per-scope read/write keys, per-name `Ed25519Signer`s, writer pseudonym signers — the seeded per-scope derivation with key-regression epochs.
- Live-session wiring: the resolve path, the held-record set, liveness-loop composition, and rehydrate-on-boot.
- Determinism preserved: entropy/time enter via seam traits, never a direct clock/RNG.

## Dependencies

**Depends on (upstream):**

- #624 — identity auth, refresh rotation, ops baseline (merged).
- #623 — facade scaffold + frozen `Engine::start` surface (merged).

## Notes

- Referenced by #697 / #739 as "the deferred facade skeleton."
- Consumed downstream by the web shell (#642, #643) and desktop login (#650), which drive the facad

You are implementing GitHub issue #870 in the CipherBox repo (FSM1/cipher-box), on branch `feat/870-vault-settings-record` forked from `main` at `082662c6a`. You are in your own git worktree — do all work there, never touch the user's main checkout, never push to `main`.

## Step 0 — read the ground truth first

- `AGENTS.md` (MANDATORY — the critical security rules, the comment discipline, rule 8 encode/decode fail-closed symmetry)
- `CONTEXT.md` (v2 ubiquitous language — use these terms exactly)

## The work

Vault settings become a **published record on the network**, resolvable with no CipherBox infrastructure. This deliberately overturns #822's `PUT/GET /account/settings`: `AGENTS.md` commits to the network being canonical and CipherBox infra being accelerator-only, and holding `ByoIpfsConfig` on the API is circular — a self-hosting user would need CipherBox to tell them where their own node is.

- Published under the name derived from the **`settings-ipns-keypair`** KDF edge (landed in #861), sealed **HPKE-to-self under `enc-subkey`**. Both derive from `loginSecret`, so the record is readable at cold start **before any vault resolve**.

- Tenants of the record: `ByoIpfsConfig` (`crates/engine/src/content/provider.rs`), `PinMode`, and the retention policy.
- **Harvest v1's semantics verbatim.** Read `apps/web/src/services/vault-settings.service.ts` on branch `v1` (`git show v1:apps/web/src/services/vault-settings.service.ts`) — checking branch `v1` for reference implementations is a mandatory recon step in this repo, not optional. Reproduce: validate the decoded payload, degrade gracefully to documented defaults on **any** failure, and bound the load with a timeout. **A settings record that will not resolve must never block cold start.**

## Hard constraint from the issue

The reserved settings id is a shared constant across accounts. The *keys* separate correctly (derivation is per-account through `loginSecret`), but the **floor store keying** is the exposed surface, and that hazard belongs to #856. **Do not add a second instance of it.** If your implementation would introduce another shared-constant floor-store key, stop and report rather than working around it.

## Acceptance (all must be covered by tests)

- Settings round-trip: written on device A, resolved on device B, opened under `enc-subkey`.
- A missing settings record yields **defaults, not an error**.
- An unresolvable settings name does not block cold start past the timeout.

Gate: `Engine Tests`. Per `blueprint/testing.md` law 1, the suite must block a merge in a named CI gate the day it lands — verify that gate exists. Assert behavior, never source text.

## Hard constraints (do not rediscover these)

- **`cargo fmt --all`** — never scope fmt to `-p <crate>`; CI runs `cargo fmt --all --check` and a scoped run has broken PRs here before.
- `cargo check --workspace` does NOT build wasm32. If you touch any seam trait bound or facade surface, also run `cargo check -p cipherbox-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- **Determinism is injected**: entropy, time and policy enter as parameters/seam traits — never call a clock or RNG directly in engine logic. The timeout above must come through a seam, not a real clock.
- **All crypto lives in `crates/core`** — no crypto in TypeScript, and no key derivation outside the frozen KDF edge catalog. `settings-ipns-keypair` and `enc-subkey` already exist; do not mint new edges.
- **v2 is greenfield**: no backward-compat arms, no `serde(default)` compat shims, no migration paths.
- **Encode/decode fail-closed symmetry (AGENTS.md rule 8):** if a decode path hard-rejects an invariant, the matching encode path must enforce it with a **release-active** check returning `Err` — never `debug_assert!`/`assert!`. Follow the `crates/core/src/seal/body.rs` `assert_children_unique` convention and cover it with a test that fires in a release build.

- `gh` requires `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN` as a prefix, always.
- Conventional Commits, **no parenthesized text in the subject line**. Commit signing goes through the 1Password SSH agent and can hang — run commits via a background/unsandboxed Bash call with a `timeout` guard, NEVER `--no-gpg-sign`. If a commit helper reports failure, verify with `git log` before retrying.

PR #897 (`feat/884-combined-move-intent-op`) is green and about to merge; it touches `crates/engine/src/sync/{drain,rebase,op,overlay}.rs` and `facade.rs`. Keep your diff out of those files as far as the slice allows, and expect to rebase onto a newer `main` before merge. Do not implement anything belonging to #868 (write file content end to end) — that is the next critical-path slice and is not yours.

## Ship flow (mandatory, in this order)

1. Implement + tests. `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, and the wasm32 check all green.
2. Open the PR as a **DRAFT** (`gh pr create --draft`). Conventional Commits title, no parens. Body: `Closes #870`, `Part of #655`. **No Claude/AI attribution footer and no session link.**
3. Run the review gates on your own diff (`git diff main...HEAD`), folding real findings back into code and tests:
   - `/simplify`
   - `/security-review`
   - `/crypto-privacy-review` — **REQUIRED**: this diff seals under `enc-subkey`, derives a published name, and adds a cold-start read path.
   If a slash-command skill is unavailable, do a rigorous manual pass against that checklist instead. Never skip a gate.
4. Leave the PR in **draft**. Do NOT mark it ready and do NOT request a CodeRabbit review — CR is rate-limited 1/hr org-wide and the user sequences it manually.

## Follow-ups

Implement small in-scope things now; otherwise fold into an existing OPEN issue; mint a NEW issue only as a last resort (`env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh issue create --label v2-build`), and every new deferred issue needs an immediate bidirectional dependency edge or it orphans.

Terse: branch, PR number, what landed, what you harvested from `v1` and where it differs, how the timeout enters through a seam, confirmation you did not add a second shared-constant floor-store key, gate results (report failures honestly with output), review-gate findings folded in, and anything left out and why. content.content:
069f2147b feat(engine): add a combined move intent op so a kernel rename is one entry (#897)
OPEN engine: write file content end to end
===== #868 full body =====
Content bytes flow: sliced by the client, sealed and staged by the engine, uploaded at drain, published as a version. Gives `ApiClient::upload` its first production caller and the contract suite its first live write coverage. Slice settled by #825 on wayfinder map #813.

## Scope

**Facade write handles** (#815). The client slices the `File` and feeds chunks; the engine seals and stages each, owning framing policy; the op is journaled once at commit. Peak wasm heap is O(chunk). This replaces `Command::Create { content: Option<PlaintextContent> }` (`facade.rs:238-247`).

**Budget admission** (#828, #829). Reserve at `beginWrite` against an exact sealed total (`size + 40n + root_len`) in an in-memory ledger of live handles, so concurrent handles cannot over-admit. `pushChunk` enforces the declared shape and never re-checks the budget. The over-budget check quotes **`budget - staged`**, never `budget`, in distinct messages for the hard limit, a transient backlog, and a device-constrained budget — they need different user actions.

**Per-block staging** (#828). A version stages as N+1 independent blocks, each keyed by its own content address; the op carries the root's, which is also the version's `contentCid`. Leaf keys are derivable by decoding the staged root. Blocks are **CID-verified on read from staging** — the read path already hard-rejects a mismatch, so an unverified upload turns bit-rot into a permanently unreadable published version.

**The per-version content key** (#818). Staged sealed, HPKE-to-self under the owner `enc-subkey`, riding the op. `enc-subkey` comes from the loginSecret, so it is epoch-independent and available exactly when a drain can run. Epoch rides the AAD as a value, not a key input. Needs a distinct struct tag and the `contentCid` in the sealed payload. A key-open failure dead-letters the op and **releases** its blocks.

**Drain upload.** File order, root last, removing each block on a confirmed `UploadResult`, so present blocks are always a **suffix** — a hole is loss, not progress, and fails closed. Upload then publish; do not pre-register CIDs, since `NameRegistration` has no CID-only form and would mint a null-head name-inventory row on every new-file write.

**The remaining two encode-side guards** (#823), both structural: one `NodeKind` feeds both the sealed body variant and `ChildRef.kind`; `SealedContent` gains `size` so the `Version` is built from one value.

**`content_cids` threaded into held records** (#797) so `eol_renew_pass` re-pins content on sub-EOL renewal.

**The observed size** (#830) is the Sigma `pushChunk` total, cross-checked against the `beginWrite` declaration and fail-closed — the reachable mismatch is a mid-upload truncation of the backing `File`, which would otherwise publish a short version as a success.

## Acceptance

- `write_plane.rs`: a file create round-trips to a second device that downloads and verifies the bytes.
- A **live contract-suite leg**: hosted upload then register then retire against a real API.
- A truncated `File` fails the commit rather than publishing a short version.

## Gate

`Engine Tests`, `Contract Suite`.

## Dependencies

Depends on #867 (the drain failure-policy slice). The content format freeze (#862) landed with PR #877.

Blocks #869, #871, #873, #896, #860 and #846.

Closes #812, #797
Part of #655

   - `generateFileKey()` produces a fresh AES-256 key per upload (per version — re-upload generates a new key, never reuses).
   - The key is ECIES-wrapped to the user's secp256k1 vault pubkey (`wrapKey`), hex-encoded, and stored as `fileKeyEncrypted` (+ `fileIv`) inside the **file metadata JSON**, which is itself AES-encrypted with the **parent folder key** and pinned to IPFS; the metadata CID is published under a per-file Ed25519 IPNS name.

content.content:
===== #880 =====
## Problem

Every rendered read now runs a full HPKE open per queued op, with no caching.

Before #864 the op queue decoded with `serde_json`. After it, `RecordReader::classify` runs, per record the session owns, an X25519 DHKEM decap plus the HKDF-SHA256 key schedule plus an XChaCha20-Poly1305 decrypt. That happens inside `Engine::scan_queue`, which is called from:

- `snapshot()` — every folder paint,
- `render()` / `rendered_snapshot()` — every view read,
- the content-read miss path.

None of them memoize. The op queue is deliberately uncapped — `crates/engine/src/sync/staging.rs`: "the op queue is the durable divergence and must never be capped" — so the per-render cost grows without bound with a user's offline backlog.

## Impact

A user offline long enough to queue a few thousand metadata ops turns each UI paint into thousands of scalar multiplications on the wasm worker thread. Retained records short-circuit cheaply before the open, so the expensive class is precisely the live account's own queue.

There is also a cheap local amplification: records bearing the victim's `ownerTag` with garbage ciphertext pay the **full** decap before failing at the AEAD tag, and they survive until the next cold start dead-letters them. Rendering, not just booting, pays for them.

## Fix

Memoize the `QueueScan` and invalidate it on enqueue and remove, so the cost is one pass per boot plus one per mutation rather than one per render. The scan is already a single struct with all three outputs, so the cache has one owner.

Care needed on invalidation: `stage_op` writes through the `StagingStore` seam directly, so the engine must not cache behind a mutation path it does not observe. Keying on the durable queue's `OpId` high-water plus length is the cheap conservative option.

## Related

Not a correctness defect — every read returns the right answer today. Filed because the cost is unbounded in a quantity the design refuses to bound.

You were right to push. Two unblocked write-plane issues I skipped:

**#880 — cache the queue scan.** I mentioned it in my very first frontier answer and then never revisited it. Its only dependency was #864, which merged as PR #878. It's a genuine unbounded-cost problem: since #864 replaced `serde_json` queue decoding with `RecordReader::classify`, every rendered read runs a full X25519 DHKEM decap plus HKDF-SHA256 schedule plus XChaCha20-Poly1305 decrypt **per queued op**, from `snapshot()`, `render()`/`rendered_snapshot()` and the content-read-miss path — none memoized. The op queue is deliberately uncapped ("the durable divergence must never be capped"), so a user offline long enough to queue a few thousand metadata ops turns every UI paint into thousands of scalar multiplications on the wasm worker thread. There's also a local amplification worth noting: records bearing the victim's `ownerTag` with garbage ciphertext pay the *full* decap before failing at the AEAD tag, and survive until the next cold start.

**#895 — the two-device deep-create assertion.** Its blockers were #867 and #884; both merged today, so it's now clear. Test-only, ~20 lines.

**But I can't launch either right now without a collision.** `#880`'s surface is `sync/{mod,record,rebase,drain}.rs` plus `facade.rs`, and `#895` is `crates/engine/tests/write_plane.rs` — which is exactly where the #868 worker is operating. #868 replaces `Command::Create`, adds the drain upload path, and adds write_plane tests. Launching either now means a three-way rebase in the repo's highest-traffic files.

Three others looked unblocked but aren't independently actionable: **#853** is already claimed by #869 (`Closes #853`), and **#860** and **#846** both gate on #868 per the edges we added earlier.

So the honest answer is: the write plane has two more items ready, and both are **queued behind #868 rather than parallelisable with it**. #880 is the more valuable of the two and is a good candidate the moment #868 lands — or now, if you'd rather I launch it and accept the rebase, since its logic is genuinely independent of #868's.

<result>## Findings

### 1. Login-secret KDF derivations — count is already minimal

`/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-ac147f524a17e1d00/crates/engine/src/settings.rs:236-237` (load) and `:186,197` (publish).

Each call derives exactly two edges: `kdf::enc_subkey` and `kdf::settings_ipns_keypair`. No re-derivation inside the loop, and `publish_settings` correctly inlines the name derivation instead of calling `settings_name()` (which would have derived the signer a second time). Cost per call: 2 BLAKE3 derives + one Ed25519 `SigningKey::from_bytes` (a scalar mult, ~50 µs; `verifying_key()` afterwards is a free copy — dalek precomputes it). **Nothing to fix.**

Minor note only: `settings_name` builds a full `Ed25519Signer` to read a public key. Unavoidable given the `kdf` API, once per cold start. Negligible.

### 2. The record is unmarshalled and Ed25519-verified twice per load — the one real redundancy

`settings.rs:257` gets `(sequence, record_bytes)` from `fanout_get_verify`, which already ran `IpnsRecord::unmarshal` + `record.verify(name)` on those exact bytes (`crates/engine/src/net/fanout.rs:101-106`). Then `fetch_head_block` (`settings.rs:298-300`) redoes both.

- Cost: one extra Ed25519 signature verification (~40–70 µs), one protobuf reparse that heap-allocates a `Vec<u8>` per field (`ProtoField.raw`), and one extra DAG-CBOR decode of the signed `data`. All the information wanted (`verified.value`) was already computed and thrown away.
- Cheaper: have the fanout hand back the `VerifiedRecord` (or just its `value`) alongside the sequence, so `fetch_head_block` takes a `&[u8]` value rather than raw record bytes.
- Verdict: **negligible in wall-clock terms** next to the network I/O around it (~0.1 ms against a 10 s budget). Worth doing only as an API-shape cleanup, not as a perf fix. Flagging it because it's the only genuinely duplicated computation the diff introduces.

### 3. `floor::sequence_floor` is serialized behind the fanout for no data dependency

`settings.rs:264` — the floor read only needs `key` (= the name), which is known at `:236`, yet it runs after `fanout_get_verify` completes. Only the *comparison* at `:267` needs the sequence.

- Cost: the FloorStore round trip (IndexedDB on web, disk on desktop — single-digit ms) is added to the budget instead of hidden under the fanout's hundreds of ms.
- Cheaper: poll the floor read concurrently with the fanout (the engine already has the pattern — `fanout_put` at `net/fanout.rs:49` hand-rolls a concurrent `poll_fn`).
- Verdict: real but small. Worth it only if `FloorStore` is slow on some host; otherwise leave it — the sequential form is the more readable one and this runs once.

The head-block read at `:271` genuinely *cannot* overlap with the fanout (its CID lives inside the record), so no opportunity there.

### 4. The dominant cold-start cost is the sequential fanout the new caller inherits

`crates/engine/src/net/fanout.rs:97-113` (not in the diff): `fanout_get_verify` awaits each endpoint's `get_record` in turn, unlike its sibling `fanout_put` which polls all endpoints concurrently.

- Cost on this new path: N sequential RTTs, and one endpoint that hangs consumes the entire `settings_load_budget` — so `load_settings` returns `Defaults(TimedOut)` even when a healthy endpoint held the record. That is the whole latency story for `load_settings`; everything else in this review is noise beside it.
- Cheaper: mirror `fanout_put`'s concurrent `poll_fn` (poll all, keep the highest sequence, settle when all settle).
- Out of the diff's scope, but the diff is what makes this a cold-start blocking path.

`read_block` (`crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:202`) rotates gateway sources sequentially too — same shape, same pre-existing caveat.

### 5. `within` does not over-poll

`settings.rs:311-323`. `Scheduler::sleep` is an `async fn`, so the timer future is inert until first polled, and it is only polled after `work` returns `Pending` — a synchronously-completing `work` never arms a timer. On a timer wakeup, `work` gets exactly one extra poll before `expiry` returns `Ready`. That is the minimum a select of two futures can do without separate wakers. **No change warranted.**

(Only theoretical cost: each wakeup re-polls `expiry`, which a badly-written host seam could re-arm a `setTimeout` on. That's a seam-implementation concern, not this combinator's.)

### 6. Body codec clones — all negligible, do not "fix"

- `settings.rs:481` — `req(&byo, "endpoint")?.as_text()?.to_string()` copies the endpoint string, while the adjacent `accessToken` at `:470-480` correctly *moves* out via `byo.remove`. Asymmetric, but a short URL; a `remove("endpoint")` would need the reads reordered.
- `settings.rs:392,412` — `kind_str(..).to_string()` / `pin_mode_str(..).to_string()` allocate a `String` per `&'static str`. Publish path only, two allocations.
- `settings.rs:501` — `key.clone()` in `reject_unknown_keys` is on the error path only; the happy path allocates nothing.
- `crates/core/src/seal/settings_record.rs:121` + `:55` — the 32-byte `owner_tag` is copied twice (`to_vec()` into the header, then `.clone()` into the AAD array). 64 bytes.
- `settings_record.rs:118` — `.map(|(key,_)| key.clone())` likewise fires only on the malformed path.

All of the above are sub-microsecond, once per cold start. Leave them.

### 7. `preflight_settings` double-work is intentional, not waste

`crates/engine/src/net/record_publish.rs:112-119` takes `block: Vec<u8>` by value (no clone — good) but re-runs a full CBOR decode + HPKE auth-decap (2 X25519 DH) + AEAD open on bytes just sealed at `settings.rs:187`. That roughly doubles the publish path's crypto (~0.3 ms → ~0.6 ms). It is the diff's stated fail-closed guarantee (AGENTS.md rule 8, and `PreflightedHead` has no other constructor). Publish is not a cold-start path. **Do not optimize.**

### Summary

Only item 4 (and secondarily 3) has measurable effect on cold start, and item 4 is pre-existing code the diff newly depends on. Items 1, 5, 6, 7 are already efficient or negligibly cheap; item 2 is a genuine redundancy but a micro one, worth fixing as an interface cleanup rather than for speed.</result>

<result>## Findings

### HIGH — 1. `publish_settings` never self-adopts and never checks the publish verdict: every second settings update silently fails to land
`crates/engine/src/settings.rs:199-215`

`publish_record` returns a `PublishReceipt`, and `publish_settings` maps only the *error* and hands the receipt back — `PublishOutcome::Unconfirmed` / `LostRace` are returned as `Ok`. It also never raises the per-name sequence floor after a confirmed publish, unlike every other caller of this port (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:1290-1299` treats `Unconfirmed`/`LostRace` as a halt, and `:1210-1226` self-adopts the returned bytes, which is what advances the floor).

Concrete failure: `publish` mints `sequence = sequence_floor(name).unwrap_or(0).max(min)+1` (`crates/engine/src/net/publish.rs:172-178`). Because nothing raises that floor on the publishing device, **two settings publishes without an intervening successful `load_settings` both mint the same sequence.** The second record collides with the first at seq N+1; confirm-by-re-resolve sees "same sequence, different bytes" → `Unconfirmed` → `publish_settings` returns `Ok(receipt)` and the caller believes the update landed. The network keeps whichever copy each endpoint holds.

Security impact, not just correctness: this is the revocation path for a BYO credential. An owner whose `access_token` leaked changes it, sees success, and the old record with the old token keeps resolving on every other device. It also leaves the publishing device's own settings floor permanently at 0/stale, so that device will happily accept a rollback to any older record of its own.

Fix: mirror `drain.rs` — match the outcome, return `Err` (a new `SettingsPublishError::Unconfirmed { sequence }`) on `Unconfirmed`/`LostRace`, and on `Published { sequence }` call `floor::advance_sequence_on_unseal(floors, name.as_str().as_bytes(), sequence)` before returning.

---

### HIGH — 2. A withheld settings record is indistinguishable from "never configured": silent downgrade to hosted pinning, and a detected rollback is reported as generic unreadability
`crates/engine/src/settings.rs:257-269`

`resolve_settings` returns `Defaults(NoRecord)` at line 258 **before it ever reads the floor**. The durable sequence floor is exactly the local, durable proof that this account *has* published settings — and it is not consulted on the suppression path.

Attack (attacker controls the record-plane endpoints, or is just on-path): withhold the record. `fanout_get_verify` returns `None` → `VaultSettings::default()` → `pin_mode: Hosted`, `byo: None`. A member who deliberately chose `PinMode::External` ("never put my bytes in CipherBox's store") is silently reverted to hosted pinning with no signal. Same outcome via any transient gateway failure on the head-block fetch (line 271). The bytes are E2EE, but the placement policy, the quota accounting, and the metadata destination are all the user's explicit choice being reverted by an attacker who only needs to drop packets.

Second half: the rollback branch at line 267-269 is a *detected trust violation* (a record cryptographically signed by the owner's settings key, at a sequence below the durable floor — nothing but a replay produces that) and it collapses into the same `DefaultsReason::Unreadable` as "the gateway 404'd". AGENTS.md rule 6: a floor violation is a fail-closed trust violation, never mere staleness. The host cannot distinguish "no settings yet" from "someone is rolling you back," so it cannot surface or act on it.

Fix: (a) read `sequence_floor` first; if it is `Some(_)` and the load produces no usable record, return a distinct host-visible reason (`Suppressed`) rather than the "first run" defaults — and prefer a durable last-known-good settings copy over silently reverting `External`→`Hosted`; (b) split the rollback into its own `DefaultsReason::Rolledback { floor, sequence }` so it is reportable.

---

### MEDIUM — 3. The published settings block stamps the owner's raw enc-subkey public half in the clear, on a block the CipherBox API pins
`crates/core/src/seal/settings_record.rs:38-43`, `:88`

`ownerTag` is `owner_enc_pub.to_bytes()` verbatim, in the clear, in a block that `publish_record` uploads to the API (`crates/engine/src/net/record_publish.rs:175-184`) and registers under the account's authenticated session. The rest of the system treats this value as sensitive: grant blobs address recipients by a **blinded** recipient tag precisely so the raw key is not a public correlator (`crates/core/src/seal/structure.rs:27`), and the enc-subkey public half is otherwise disclosed only by deliberate out-of-band contact-code exchange (`crates/engine/src/grants/contact.rs:27-40`).

Consequence: the zero-knowledge API operator holds `account → settings ipnsName → head block → raw X25519 enc pubkey`, and so can link an account identity to the long-term key any contact-code holder also knows. It also makes every settings republish publicly linkable to the same owner.

The tag buys nothing on this record. The reader is the owner, who already has the key, and `open_settings_record` re-derives the tag from the caller's own secret and compares (`:132-135`) — it is never used for lookup or routing. Fix: drop it from the clear header (bind the version + a constant in the AAD), or carry a blinded tag consistent with the grant family. If it stays, the module header should say why a published record may expose what grants deliberately blind.

---

### MEDIUM — 4. The BYO access token is dropped un-zeroized on one decode error path
`crates/engine/src/settings.rs:452`, `:463-469`

`read_settings_map` detaches the `byo` submap from the tree with `map.remove("byo")` at line 452, so the later `tree.zeroize_bytes()` in `decode_settings_body` (line 423) no longer covers it. Inside `read_byo`, `reject_unknown_keys(&byo, &BYO_KEYS)?` at line 469 can return `Err` **before** `accessToken` is moved into its `Zeroizing` owner at line 478 — the local `Map` still holds `Value::Text(<token>)` and is dropped with a plain `String` drop, leaving the credential in freed heap. (The `endpoint`/`kind` failure paths at 481-486 are clean: the token has already moved into `Zeroizing` by then and zeroizes on unwind.)

Fix: make `read_byo` the terminal owner of the detached subtree — run the body in an inner closure, `byo.zeroize_bytes()` on every exit, then return the result, exactly as `decode_settings_body` does for `tree`.

---

### MEDIUM — 5. `validate_endpoint` is too weak to be the only gate on a record-sourced endpoint
`crates/engine/src/content/provider.rs:120-130`, called from `crates/engine/src/settings.rs:366`

It is a scheme+non-empty-authority prefix check and nothing more. It closes `file:`/relative/hostless (its stated job for a member typing into a form) but does **not** close:

- **Plaintext `http://` carrying a bearer.** `probe_request` attaches `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to whatever URL it is given (`provider.rs:143-148`); `http://kubo.example` is accepted, so the credential goes over cleartext to an arbitrary host. `a_local_http_kubo_endpoint_is_allowed` shows plaintext is intentional — but it should be intentional *for loopback*, not for the public internet.
- **Control characters / whitespace in the authority.** `"http://host\r\nX-Evil: 1"` passes, and the string is spliced into a request URL by `format!("{base}{path}")`. Whether that becomes header injection depends entirely on the host `Http` seam (native reqwest vs a browser `fetch` shim behave differently) — the engine should not be delegating that.
- **`@` userinfo, `?`, `#`** in the "authority", which reshape the effective request target.
- **Loopback / link-local / cloud-metadata (`169.254.169.254`) targets.** Self-inflicted for a live member, but on this path the endpoint arrives from a *decoded record* — including, on a device with no floor yet, an old record replayed by the network (finding 2). "Point every content write at 127.0.0.1 and watch uploads fail" is a cheap availability attack with no user-visible cause.

Fix: tighten `validate_endpoint` into a real allowlist — reject any byte outside the unreserved URL host/port set (no ASCII control, no whitespace, no `@ ? # \ [ ]`), require `https` unless the host resolves to loopback, and add an explicit loopback/link-local/private-range decision rather than leaving it unstated.

---

### LOW — 6. A floor-store write failure downgrades a fully verified record to defaults
`crates/engine/src/settings.rs:282-287`

The record verified, opened, and validated; only the durable floor raise failed (host I/O — an availability event, never a trust verdict, per the convention in `net/publish.rs:125-128`). Returning `Defaults(Unreadable)` throws away known-good settings and applies the hosted-pinning default because a disk write failed. Fix: return `Resolved(settings)` and report the floor-raise failure separately, or at minimum use a reason that does not read as "your record is bad."

### LOW — 7. No sanity check on the injected HPKE ephemeral before it reaches the public network
`crates/engine/src/settings.rs:182-185`

`seal_settings_record`'s contract is "fresh per record — reuse is a confidentiality break," and `hpke_seal_auth` performs no scalar validation (`crates/core/src/suite/hpke.rs:116-129`). A host `Entropy` seam that returns `Ok(())` having written zeros (a plausible WASM/CSPRNG-unavailable failure mode) silently produces a fixed ephemeral across every settings version, and unlike the op record these are published where the reuse is externally observable. A release-active all-zero reject before the seal is ~free.

### LOW — 8. The resolved settings record's EOL is never checked
`crates/engine/src/settings.rs:257`, `:298-300`

`fanout_get_verify` and `IpnsRecord::verify` check the signature chain only; `verified.validity` is available and ignored, and `eol::is_expired` is used nowhere in the resolve path (only `liveness.rs:193`). So a long-expired settings record is honored indefinitely. This is consistent with the rest of the engine's resolve path — but on *this* record the stale content re-points where bytes get stored and which credential is presented, so it is the worst place to inherit the omission.

### LOW — 9. The publish path has no time budget
`crates/engine/src/settings.rs:164-215`

`load_settings` is bounded by `settings_load_budget`; `publish_settings` is unbounded. If every record endpoint hangs without settling, `fanout_put` never returns. Pre-existing in the shared port, but the settings plane is the one advertised as "must never block cold start."

---

## Checked and clean

- **Forgery of the record body.** Auth-mode HPKE with the enc subkey as both static sender and recipient; `open_settings_record` re-derives `owner_enc_pub` from the caller's own secret and passes *that* as the sender (`settings_record.rs:132-146`), never the framed `ownerTag` — the caller invariant in `hpke_open_auth`'s doc is honored. The base-mode-forgery test (`:248-272`) covers the downgrade. So `endpoint` / `access_token` / `PinMode` / `keepLatest` are **not** attacker-injectable; the only network-input attacks against them are replay and suppression (findings 1, 2).
- **Every decoded body field is bound or validated.** `pinMode` and `byo.kind` are closed discriminant sets with a fail-closed `_` arm (`settings.rs:444`, `:486`); `keepLatest` is `Null|Unsigned` with `KeepLatest(0)` rejected on both sides; `byo` is `Null|Map`; unknown keys rejected at both levels (`BODY_KEYS`, `BYO_KEYS`); `endpoint` runs `validate_endpoint` (weak — finding 5); `access_token` is length-unbounded but the whole record is size-capped.
- **AAD / domain separation.** New struct tag `0x0b`, dense and in byte order, asserted at `aad.rs` (`STRUCT_TAGS.len() == 11`); distinct HPKE `info`; 4-element AAD array structurally non-unifiable with op-record's 5 and grants' 6; version bound into the AAD *and* gated before the AEAD; cross-family transplant test present.
- **Rollback ordering in `resolve_settings`.** Floor read (264) → compare (267) → fetch → open → decode → advance (282). An unopenable, mis-addressed, or malformed record cannot raise the floor. A floor the store cannot read is treated as `Unreadable`, never as "no floor." The comparison is `<` not `<=`, which correctly re-admits the device's own current record; no lockout if the budget cancels between decode and the raise. Single-writer engine, so no TOCTOU between the read and the raise.
- **Publish/read plane agreement.** `preflight_settings` computes the CID as `compute_cid(DAG_ROOT_CODEC, block)` — identical to `net/author.rs:171` — and the reader anchors `ContentPlane::Root`, whose codec is `DAG_ROOT_CODEC` (`content/read.rs:47-53`). `PreflightedHead`'s private fields keep the "no un-dry-run head reaches the network" invariant intact. The block is reopened under the same enc secret the reader will use before it ships.
- **Encode/decode symmetry (rule 8).** `validate()` is literally the same predicate on both sides, release-active `Err` on the encode side, with a test that hand-encodes past the guard and asserts the reader reaches the identical verdict. Size is capped at `MAX_RESOLVED_RECORD_BYTES` on the publish side against the same constant `read_block` enforces.
- **DoS bounds.** Block size capped on both sides at 4 MiB, enforced at the transport (`send_capped`) plus a backstop on the body length; CBOR decode is depth-limited (`codec/decode.rs:150-151`); the resolve is bounded end-to-end by the scheduler budget; the head block is CID-verified before decode, so a malicious gateway cannot choose the bytes fed to `decode` at all.
- **Determinism seams.** No `SystemTime`, no RNG, no `Instant` in either new module. Entropy arrives via `Entropy::fill`; time only via `Scheduler::sleep`/`now`. `within()` (`settings.rs:311-323`) is correct: work is polled first, the expiry only when work pends, both wakers registered, no busy-spin, and it still fires if the work future fails to register a waker.
- **`Debug` redaction.** `ByoIpfsConfig`'s hand-written redacting `Debug` still holds (test at `provider.rs:286-295`), and every new `Debug`-deriving type that transitively contains it (`VaultSettings`, `SettingsLoad`, `SettingsInvalid`, `SettingsPublishError`, `BodyError`) inherits the redaction. Nothing logs. `PreflightError`'s `Display` prints only `CodecError::check()` codes.
- **Encode-side token handling.** The transient `Value` tree is wiped at `settings.rs:417` on both the success *and* the `encode`-error path, and the returned buffer is a `Zeroizing`. Decode-side success path moves the token `String` into `Zeroizing` rather than copying it (`:478`). Only the one error path in finding 4 escapes.
- **Multi-account / #856.** The settings floor key is `name.as_str().as_bytes()` (`settings.rs:260`) — the IPNS name of the `settings-ipns-keypair` edge, a pure function of the login secret, verified distinct per account by `the_settings_name_is_derived_from_the_login_secret_alone`. That is the `sequence_floor` namespace, which #856 explicitly exempts ("sequence floors key on `ipnsName`, which is globally unique"). **No shared-constant floor key is introduced**, and no epoch floor is touched at all — the settings record carries no scope and no epoch. Clean.
- **`Value::zeroize_bytes` widened to `pub`.** No downside: it recurses correctly through `Array` and `Map`, and it only ever scrubs.</result>

<result>## Findings

### HIGH — 1. `publish_settings` never self-adopts and never checks the publish verdict: every second settings update silently fails to land
`crates/engine/src/settings.rs:199-215`

`publish_record` returns a `PublishReceipt`, and `publish_settings` maps only the *error* and hands the receipt back — `PublishOutcome::Unconfirmed` / `LostRace` are returned as `Ok`. It also never raises the per-name sequence floor after a confirmed publish, unlike every other caller of this port (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:1290-1299` treats `Unconfirmed`/`LostRace` as a halt, and `:1210-1226` self-adopts the returned bytes, which is what advances the floor).

Concrete failure: `publish` mints `sequence = sequence_floor(name).unwrap_or(0).max(min)+1` (`crates/engine/src/net/publish.rs:172-178`). Because nothing raises that floor on the publishing device, **two settings publishes without an intervening successful `load_settings` both mint the same sequence.** The second record collides with the first at seq N+1; confirm-by-re-resolve sees "same sequence, different bytes" → `Unconfirmed` → `publish_settings` returns `Ok(receipt)` and the caller believes the update landed. The network keeps whichever copy each endpoint holds.

Security impact, not just correctness: this is the revocation path for a BYO credential. An owner whose `access_token` leaked changes it, sees success, and the old record with the old token keeps resolving on every other device. It also leaves the publishing device's own settings floor permanently at 0/stale, so that device will happily accept a rollback to any older record of its own.

Fix: mirror `drain.rs` — match the outcome, return `Err` (a new `SettingsPublishError::Unconfirmed { sequence }`) on `Unconfirmed`/`LostRace`, and on `Published { sequence }` call `floor::advance_sequence_on_unseal(floors, name.as_str().as_bytes(), sequence)` before returning.

---

### HIGH — 2. A withheld settings record is indistinguishable from "never configured": silent downgrade to hosted pinning, and a detected rollback is reported as generic unreadability
`crates/engine/src/settings.rs:257-269`

`resolve_settings` returns `Defaults(NoRecord)` at line 258 **before it ever reads the floor**. The durable sequence floor is exactly the local, durable proof that this account *has* published settings — and it is not consulted on the suppression path.

Attack (attacker controls the record-plane endpoints, or is just on-path): withhold the record. `fanout_get_verify` returns `None` → `VaultSettings::default()` → `pin_mode: Hosted`, `byo: None`. A member who deliberately chose `PinMode::External` ("never put my bytes in CipherBox's store") is silently reverted to hosted pinning with no signal. Same outcome via any transient gateway failure on the head-block fetch (line 271). The bytes are E2EE, but the placement policy, the quota accounting, and the metadata destination are all the user's explicit choice being reverted by an attacker who only needs to drop packets.

Second half: the rollback branch at line 267-269 is a *detected trust violation* (a record cryptographically signed by the owner's settings key, at a sequence below the durable floor — nothing but a replay produces that) and it collapses into the same `DefaultsReason::Unreadable` as "the gateway 404'd". AGENTS.md rule 6: a floor violation is a fail-closed trust violation, never mere staleness. The host cannot distinguish "no settings yet" from "someone is rolling you back," so it cannot surface or act on it.

Fix: (a) read `sequence_floor` first; if it is `Some(_)` and the load produces no usable record, return a distinct host-visible reason (`Suppressed`) rather than the "first run" defaults — and prefer a durable last-known-good settings copy over silently reverting `External`→`Hosted`; (b) split the rollback into its own `DefaultsReason::Rolledback { floor, sequence }` so it is reportable.

### MEDIUM — 3. The published settings block stamps the owner's raw enc-subkey public half in the clear, on a block the CipherBox API pins
`crates/core/src/seal/settings_record.rs:38-43`, `:88`

`ownerTag` is `owner_enc_pub.to_bytes()` verbatim, in the clear, in a block that `publish_record` uploads to the API (`crates/engine/src/net/record_publish.rs:175-184`) and registers under the account's authenticated session. The rest of the system treats this value as sensitive: grant blobs address recipients by a **blinded** recipient tag precisely so the raw key is not a public correlator (`crates/core/src/seal/structure.rs:27`), and the enc-subkey public half is otherwise disclosed only by deliberate out-of-band contact-code exchange (`crates/engine/src/grants/contact.rs:27-40`).

Consequence: the zero-knowledge API operator holds `account → settings ipnsName → head block → raw X25519 enc pubkey`, and so can link an account identity to the long-term key any contact-code holder also knows. It also makes every settings republish publicly linkable to the same owner.

The tag buys nothing on this record. The reader is the owner, who already has the key, and `open_settings_record` re-derives the tag from the caller's own secret and compares (`:132-135`) — it is never used for lookup or routing. Fix: drop it from the clear header (bind the version + a constant in the AAD), or carry a blinded tag consistent with the grant family. If it stays, the module header should say why a published record may expose what grants deliberately blind.

### MEDIUM — 4. The BYO access token is dropped un-zeroized on one decode error path
`crates/engine/src/settings.rs:452`, `:463-469`

`read_settings_map` detaches the `byo` submap from the tree with `map.remove("byo")` at line 452, so the later `tree.zeroize_bytes()` in `decode_settings_body` (line 423) no longer covers it. Inside `read_byo`, `reject_unknown_keys(&byo, &BYO_KEYS)?` at line 469 can return `Err` **before** `accessToken` is moved into its `Zeroizing` owner at line 478 — the local `Map` still holds `Value::Text(<token>)` and is dropped with a plain `String` drop, leaving the credential in freed heap. (The `endpoint`/`kind` failure paths at 481-486 are clean: the token has already moved into `Zeroizing` by then and zeroizes on unwind.)

Fix: make `read_byo` the terminal owner of the detached subtree — run the body in an inner closure, `byo.zeroize_bytes()` on every exit, then return the result, exactly as `decode_settings_body` does for `tree`.
